security_audit.summary: Most static filesystem and command findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, code fences, inline field names, and templates. Confirmed risks are limited to a connector command that fetches user-controlled URLs and a mutable raw GitHub fallback; semantic review also found automatic memory persistence that needs safeguards.

remediation.issue: Connector command accepts a user-provided URL in a shell example.
remediation.suggestion: Quote the URL argument in the command example and require the connector to reject localhost, private IP ranges, and non-HTTP schemes before fetching.

remediation.issue: Standalone fallback loads instruction files from a mutable GitHub main branch.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the runbook with the skill, or pin remote fallback URLs to a release tag and verify a documented content hash before use.

remediation.issue: Audit results are promoted to persistent memory without user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before writing hot-cache or open-loop memory, and strip raw untrusted page text from saved summaries.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instruction Fallback
semantic_findings.description: The standalone fallback tells agents to fetch runbook and reference instructions from raw.githubusercontent.com on the main branch. Mutable remote Markdown can change skill behavior after marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly names a raw GitHub main-branch fallback for instruction files. The risk is contextual supply-chain drift rather than direct exfiltration, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Persistent Memory Writes From Audit Results
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to promote audit blockers into persistent memory without user confirmation. Because audited content can be untrusted, this can preserve hostile or misleading content-derived text for later agent runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 87 and 437 require persistent memory writes, and line 98 identifies fetched content as untrusted. The exact payload stored depends on runtime audit output, so the finding is medium confidence.

content.value_statement: Publishing weak content can reduce trust, search performance, and AI citation potential. This skill applies CORE-EEAT checks and returns a clear publish verdict.
actual_capabilities: Scores content against 80 CORE-EEAT checks across eight dimensions.
Flags critical veto blockers for disclosure, intent alignment, and data consistency.
Calculates GEO, SEO, dimension, and weighted total scores by content type.
Produces a SHIP, FIX, or BLOCK publish-readiness verdict.
Ranks the top improvement priorities with concrete action steps.
Supports pasted content, authorized URLs, files, and competitor comparisons.
limitations: It needs content text, a file, or an authorized URL to audit.
Some authority and trust items may be unavailable without site-level data.
Connector-based URL fetching depends on the host environment and security policy.
Scores guide content quality and do not guarantee rankings or AI citations.

use_cases.title: Pre-Publish Editorial Gate
use_cases.description: Check a draft before launch and identify blockers that need revision first.

use_cases.title: SEO Content Refresh Planning
use_cases.description: Audit an older page and rank fixes by weighted impact across CORE-EEAT dimensions.

use_cases.title: Competitive Content Benchmarking
use_cases.description: Compare a page against competitor content and find gaps in evidence, structure, and trust.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a draft and want a simple publish check.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this content against CORE-EEAT and tell me whether it is ready to publish: [paste content].

prompt_templates.title: Content Type Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: You know the page format and target topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a content quality audit for this [content type] targeting [keyword]: [URL or pasted content].

prompt_templates.title: Competitor Comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to understand why another page may perform better.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my page against this competitor page. Report score gaps, veto risks, and the top five fixes: [my content] [competitor content].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced GEO Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: You need SEO trust and AI citation readiness in one review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this draft for AI citation readiness and SEO trust. Prioritize [goal], include weighted scores, veto checks, and a handoff summary: [content].

output_examples.input: Audit a product review before launch.
output_examples.output: Verdict: FIX. Overall score is 72/100. The strongest issues are weak first-hand proof, missing source mapping, and thin disclosure placement.

output_examples.input: Compare our guide with a competitor guide.
output_examples.output: The competitor is stronger in evidence density and structure. Your fastest gains are a summary box, tighter methodology notes, and a clearer FAQ section.

output_examples.input: Check whether an updated article is ready to ship.
output_examples.output: Verdict: SHIP. No critical trust blockers were found. Re-audit after adding the planned comparison table and author review note.

best_practices: Provide the target content type, keyword, and page goal before scoring.
Include source links, author details, and disclosure context when available.
Re-run the audit after edits to confirm score movement and new risks.
anti_patterns: Do not use the score as a ranking guarantee or traffic forecast.
Do not skip veto checks because the total score looks strong.
Do not penalize site-level items when no site-level evidence is available.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits content quality, E-E-A-T signals, GEO readiness, and publish readiness using the CORE-EEAT framework.

faq.question: Can it audit a URL?
faq.answer: Yes, if the URL is user-provided or authorized and the host environment allows safe fetching.

faq.question: What verdicts can it return?
faq.answer: It returns SHIP, FIX, or BLOCK based on scores, veto checks, and output completeness.

faq.question: Does it replace an SEO technical audit?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on content quality. Use a technical SEO auditor for tags, crawlability, and site health.

faq.question: How does it handle missing data?
faq.answer: It marks unavailable items as not applicable and explains when site-level data is required.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
